Author: Chief Justice
Bench: Chief Justice, Arun Mishra

1
 In The Supreme Court Of India
 Criminal Appellate Jurisdiction
 Criminal Appeal No.694 Of 2010
 Lal Chand Dayaram ...Appellant(S)
 Versus
 State Of Gujarat ...Respondent(S)
 O R D E R
1.

This appeal is directed against the judgment and order passed by the High Court of Gujarat at Ahmedabad in Criminal Revision Application No.199 of 1999, dated 10.07.2009, whereby and whereunder the the High Court has confirmed the order of conviction and sentence passed by the Courts below for the offence punishable under Section 7(ii) read with Section 16(1) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 (for short, the PFA Act).
2. The brief facts of the prosecution case are that the Accused No.1 was an owner of a provision store and the Accused No.2 was a wholesaler.

entities.text: High Court of Gujarat at Ahmedabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Accused No.1 purchased tins of groundnut oil from Accused No.2, and kept it in his provision store for sale for human consumption.
On 24.02.1987 at about 2:00 p.m. the food inspector, in the presence of the Accused No.1 and panch witness purchased a sample of groundnut oil meant for human consumption.
3. One portion of the sample was sent to the public analyst, Vadodara for analysis.
The report of the public analyst revealed that the sample was adulterated.
The food inspector received sanction to prosecute the accused persons, and thereafter filed a complaint against the accused persons before the Trial Court.

4. Thereafter, the accused persons appeared before the Trial Court and after both sides were heard,
charges were framed.
The charges were read over and explained to the accused persons who pleaded not guilty.
Accordingly, the case was committed to Trial.

5. Upon a detailed examination of the entire evidence on record, by judgment and order dated 19.01.1991, the Trial Court convicted the Accused No.2 for the offence punishable under Section 7(ii)

1 read with Section 16(1) of the PFA Act and sentenced him to undergo imprisonment for six months,
and also to pay a fine of Rs.1,000/-, and in default to undergo imprisonment for one month.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Further, the Trial Court held that the Accused No.1 had purchased the groundnut from Accused No.2 but had failed to obtain written warranty in prescribed form regarding the nature and quality of the groundnut oil.

Hence, the Trial Court convicted the Accused No.1 for the offence punishable under Section 7(i) read with Section 16(1) of the PFA Act and sentenced him to undergo imprisonment for six months, and also to pay a fine of Rs.1,000/-, and in default to undergo imprisonment for one month.
6. Being aggrieved by the said judgment and order passed by the Trial Court, the accused persons carried the matter in appeal before the Court of Additional Sessions Judge at Vadodara.

7. Upon careful consideration of the material on record including the order passed by the Trial Court, the Additional Sessions Judge was of the considered view that there was no occasion to differ from the well reasoned judgment and order passed by the Trial Court.
Thereby, by the judgment and order dated 02.02.1999, the Additional Sessions Judge confirmed the judgment of conviction and order of sentence passed by the Trial Court against the accused persons.
8. Being aggrieved by the said judgment and order passed by the Additional Sessions Judge, the accused persons preferred Criminal Revision Applications before the High Court of Gujarat at Ahmedabad.

entities.text: High Court of Gujarat at Ahmedabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Upon careful consideration of the material on record including the judgments and orders passed by the Courts below, and after hearing the parties at length, the High Court was of the considered view that there was no merit in the criminal revision applications filed by the accused persons and dismissed the same.
9. Being aggrieved by the judgment and order passed by the High Court in Criminal Revision Application No.199 of 1999 the Accused No.2 is before us in this appeal.
10. We have heard the learned counsel for the parties to the lis.
11. The learned counsel for the Accused No.2 would assail the judgment and order passed by the High Court.
Apart from arguing on merits of the case, learned counsel for the Accused No.2 would pray for reduction in the sentence.

The learned counsel for the Accused No.2 would submit that the Accused No.2 is 65 years of age and has withdrawn from the business of selling of food articles, and keeping these aspects of the matter in view, the sentence ought to be reduced.
12. Per contra, the learned counsel appearing for the respondent-State would support the judgment of conviction and order of sentence passed by the High Court.

13. After going through the judgments and orders passed by the High Court as well as the Courts below, we are of the considered view that there is no infirmity in the well reasoned judgment of conviction and order of sentence passed by the Courts below for the offence punishable under 7(ii)
read with Section 16(1) of the PFA Act which requires our interference.
